A dual-active NTN modem can maintain two simultaneous satellite links, significantly reducing the risk ofoutages caused by shadowing, fading or interference. At the same time, it provides an additional communication channel that enables load balancing across space segmentnodes, helping to distribute traffic efficiently and improve peak user data rates. Active resource management is essential in this context. Strategies must be designed todynamically allocate resources based on real-time link conditions and performance metrics. These strategies should ensure that the satellite system can optimize keyperformance indicators, such as peak data rate and service availability, while minimizing the resources allocated to each link and network node (e.g. payloads). Developingcontrol plane methodologies is also a critical aspect of this solution. The control plane manages the signalling and control information required for the operation of thecommunication links. It enables the system to gather real-time measurements of links conditions, which are essential for making informed decisions about resource allocationand link management. These methodologies also provide mechanisms for communicating decisions to the network including satellites and user terminals ensuring that thesystem can adapt to changing conditions and maintain optimal performance.This activity will develop a prototype dual-active 5G modem, potentially based on open radio stacks, and implement a testbed to evaluate the prototype under realisticconditions. This testbed will include a channel emulator with multiple RF interfaces to emulate themultiple links. Channel performance as well as satellite system resourcesallocation will be tested for various operational scenarios, and both resource management methodologies and control plane techniques will be assessed.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl. original.description: To develop an active antenna combined software and hardware demonstrator representative of a LEO satellite payload by exploiting advanced strategies for real time dynamically managing radio resources.Description: On-board satellite resource allocationstrategiesare essential for managing the distribution of limited resources from the antennas to multiple user terminals. These strategies involve dynamic allocation techniques that can adjust in real-time based on traffic demand. However, in dense traffic scenarios like onboard LEO satellites, these strategies face significant challenges. The high volume of demand can lead to congestion, resulting in increased latency and reduced QoS. Additionally, the limited on-board processing capability challenges the satellite's ability to efficiently manage traffic which leads to degraded antenna performance. Considering these challenges, the objective of this activity isto develop an active antenna combined software and hardware demonstrator representative of a LEO satellite payload by exploiting advanced strategies for dynamically managing radio resources, i.e. beamforming for real time tracking and coverage change combined with power and bandwidth allocation. Resource allocation should be defined as an optimization problem, considering factors like channelconditions, user demands, interference levels, and power constraints. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Derive real-time complex coefficients, using optimization strategies for the beamforming network. - Emulate users' movement and channel changes for proactive beam steering. - Develop models to detect and classify interference sources and use optimization techniquesfor mitigation. - Manufacture and test a proof-of-concept hardware demonstrator with a limited size active phased array and associated adaptivebeamforming, mounted on a mechanically movable platform with additional antennas located in fixed positions.

original.description: The Strategic Advocacy Facility is a strategic Action Readiness instrument within ESA's Earth Action framework that enables the translation of EO innovation, science and applications into sustained operational uptake and impact, particularly within the impact finance ecosystem of International Financial Institutions, climate and environmental funds, and developing-country stakeholders. The Facility combines programme-level impact measurement and evidence generation, strategic partnership engagement, institutional advisorysupport, country-level uptake assessment, strategic intelligence, advocacy and communication within a single integrated framework. Building on the legacy and assets of the Global Development Assistance (GDA) programme, it establishes a common Theory of Change, monitoring and evaluation system, stakeholder engagement architecture and learning framework for Earth Action, while creating feedbackloops between implementation, partnerships, communication, programme governance and future RD investments. Through interconnected task setup, the Facility acts as a cross-cutting enabler that strengthens EO adoption, supports partner alignment, captures and communicates evidence of impact, and ensures that Earth Action activities can be scaled, mainstreamed and translated into long-term societal, environmental and development outcomes.

original.description: Objectives: To consolidate alternative solutions for on-board loss minimization. To develop the prototypes of the most relevant solutions identified, to confirm the predicted performance. To provide road-map to flight models. The state of art TTC Sub-System architectures for Science and Exploration missions are nowadays quite complex. In order to allow communications during all mission phases, several antennas are needed in combination with redundant High Power Amplifiers (HPA) and transponders (DST). The interconnectionamong these components is accomplished by the RF Distribution Unit (RFDU), which has to guarantee the maximum degree of reconfigurability and reliability to failures. In addition, it has also to implement the necessary filtering action, to allow full duplex communications. Its design is therefore quite complex encompassing the use of several switches, Diplexers, Filters and interconnecting waveguides (WG) runs. The latter can be quite long as they have to reach antennas which are typically far from the location of the rest of the TTC subsystem. All this results in high losses with RF power reduction in transmission and increased noise figure in reception.The design solutions used so far in the frame of ESA projects are quite recurrent with no major improvements in the last decades. As shown in a TTC Sub-System architecture survey carried out in 2017, different approaches exist, as identified for example by other agencies and already flown successfully in the past years. For a complex RFDU as used in Deep Space missions, we can consider RF path losses in the order of 1 to 3 dB in X-band and 3 to 4 dB in Ka-band, withsignificant impacts in terms of data return (up to50% reduction) and in terms of spacecraft recovery possibilities in case of anomalies (increasedoperations complexity and limitation on maximum achievable distance). Therefore, there is a clear need for loss reduction in the RFDU paths, through the implementation of novel solutions. A study is on-going to consolidate the possible alternative subsystem Architectures, and define relevant requirements. This will be completed in early 2024, but its conclusions need to be consolidated by experimental results. The activity shall focus on the specification, detailed design, development and tests of prototypes of the components which will have the most significant impact on the TTC subsystem performance and whose feasibility has to be demonstrated. Three main items have been already identified, which may need to be completed by additional technologies as an outcome of the on-going study:- Receiving only antenna with integrated low-noise-amplifier (LNA) and downconverter (D/C), with a possible alternative for a receiving and transmitting solution;- High-gain-antenna dual-band feed including receiving LNA and D/C, and with direct interface to power amplifier;- Transponder front-end to manage the interfaces with new antennas designs.Tasks:1. Consolidation of requirements and design2. Design and manufacturing of bread-boards3. Testing of bread-boards4. Development plan for flight models.

original.description: Today, mission ground segment systems face increasingly sophisticated and fast-movingcyber threats that can evade static or rule-based detection tools and overwhelm traditionalrecovery procedures. As attacks grow more pervasive, dynamic and subtle, currentapproaches, such as rule-based or ticket driven responses struggle to react at the requiredspeed, resulting in prolonged attacker dwelltime and potential disruption of critical missionoperations, if an attack is detected at all.Real-time automated responses or self-healing' mechanisms, such as fall-back tosecure/minimum configurations, runtime policy/rule change, trusted state reconstitution, orrapid tear-down and re-deploy of compromised systems, can reduce the time required tocontain threats. The aim is to reduce attacker dwell time and maintain service continuityduring otherwise high impact incidents. This activity addresses that gap by developing anddemonstrating a proof-of-concept autonomous self-healing architecture tailored to thecritical mission operations ground segment. It will provide an adaptive resilience mechanismaddressing detection, isolation and recovery with an emphasis on service continuity. Moderntechnologies and techniques are to be explored including:- declarative infrastructure as code for cloud-agnostic redundancy and recovery automation- decoupled micro-service isolation and zero-trust architectures- secure root of trust and immutable system configuration restoration- failure prediction- adaptive response mechanisms leveraging machine learning.The proof-of-concept demonstrator will be integrated into a multi-mission, cloud nativeground segment scenario, leveraging existing (Cyber) Security Operations Centres((C)SOC) monitoring and diagnostic capabilities to ensure operational relevance. It willdemonstrate end to enddetection, isolation, and recovery in the context of missionmonitoring and control systems operating in the loop.

The upcoming 6G NTN integration into the terrestrial telecom systemenables new features such as:a. Seamless interoperability between terrestrial and satellite networks;b. Direct-to-device connectivity without specialised satellite terminals in FR 1 (i.e., <7GHz);c. Ubiquitous connectivity across geography;d. Broadband servicesfor aviation, maritime, and cross-border mobility;e. AI-Native networking to optimise beam management, manage mobility, and dynamically allocate spectrum across the multi-layered satellitenetwork.However, today no European solution exists for a full gNB signal processing hardware platform and software protocol stack as needed for 5G/6Gregenerative NTN payloads.This activity will develop a European gNB hardware and software protocol stack architecture for regenerative NGSO satellite with a fully European signalprocessing platform, i.e., both hardware and software. The gNB shall be able to support high throughput 5G/6G connectivity either in S-band spectrum(e.g., up to 50Mbit/s) or in Ka-band spectrum (e.g., up to 1Gbit/s).The activity will: Develop a concept of an efficient signal processing hardware and software protocol stack architecture for a European gNB implementation for regenerative NGSO satellites. Identify a suitable European signal processing platform and characterise relevant functional blocks of the signal processing hardware. A laboratory breadboard will be developed together with electrical ground support equipment (EGSE) suitable to performradiation characterisation including Single Event Effects (SEE), Displacement Damage (DD), and Total Ionizing Dose (TID). A radiation mitigation approach shall be developed and implemented using a combination of software- and hardware-based solutions to compensate for identified critical performance impacts. The devicewith the applied radiation mitigation measures will be radiation tested,and the performance will be compared to the unmitigated hardware performance. Carry out analysis and concept trade-offs to ensurethehigh throughput connectivity and minimised power consumption per MHz in the selected band (S-band or Ka-band)Identify and assess relevant in-orbit experiment considerations.

original.description: The main objective of this activity is to comprehensively gather, analyse and consolidate the requirements and specifications for afuture concept of a Measurement Command  Control (MCC) system intended to support ESA propulsion test facilities[ID2.1][ID2.2][ID2.3] for systems and subsystems in a five- to ten-year timeframe. The main use case of such an MCC will be for larger test bench facilities such as the P5 at DLR Lampoldshausen and PF50 at Vernon (hundreds of simultaneous measurements within a large frequency spectrum) but shall be highly adaptable to other similar benches. The activity shall identify innovative technologies, architectural concepts, to support the following objectives:Improve Operational efficiency, maintainability, scalability and performance;SupportStandardization;Ensure energy efficiency for Sustainability purposesReduce Recurring Costs.Subsequently, the study aims to formulate a comprehensive concept for the future MCC, including preliminary system requirements, architectural definition, innovativefeatures, and an assessment of existing and emerging solutions and suppliers ideally from ESA Member States. Thus, the study shall assess the availability and maturity of the required technologies within the European ecosystem, identify potential capability gaps,and recommend developments needed to strengthen European technological autonomy, resilience, and sovereignty in this strategic domain. The resulting concept shall establish the foundations for future procurement and implementation activities across ESA propulsiontest facilities.[ID3.1][ID3.2][ID3.3] Particular attention shall be given to disruptive concepts and architectural evolutions capable of delivering a substantial leap in the bench capabilities with respect to the given objectives.
